recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not remove adr from current THO-backed consent scope/category surfaces under FHIR-23719; any new alignment work for Advance Directives, treatment directives, Consent, ServiceRequest, PACIO, or IPS should proceed through a new work-group decision such as the still-open FHIR-50903 discussion.
issue_request: FHIR-23719 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested removing Advance Directives from the Consent resource scope, removing references through Consent.scope and introductory text, and adding a note that HL7 was working on Advance Directives.
initial_application: Git commit 2da480ca699986fa93ba5f234dc5b055146d8144 explicitly listed GF#23719 and changed source/consent/consent-introduction.xml plus the old source/consent/consent-spreadsheet.xml. The current refactored Consent source has no Consent.scope element and the current introduction lists privacy, treatment, and research as the three anticipated Consent uses.
additional_context: FHIR-34215 was later Published/Persuasive to add adr back into the ConsentScope codelist, and UP-255 was implemented in THO to restore adr because R4 implementations used the code and THO had become inconsistent with the R4 code system. The related Zulip thread records that CBCC had removed Advance Directives for R5, but users were asking for restoration and scope/category were being merged. Current THO therefore intentionally includes adr; current Consent.category is an example binding that includes broader category examples, including advance-directive-related terminology.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current core Consent scope text already reflects the removal requested by FHIR-23719, while the remaining adr/category terminology reflects later final decisions rather than an unapplied deletion. Adding the 2019 note now would be stale because subsequent PACIO/ADI and terminology work exists and the page already says other use cases may be handled through category codes.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 decision to add adr back into the ConsentScope codelist after the earlier removal caused a THO/R4 validation mismatch.
Implemented THO proposal restoring adr to http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/consentscope.

Later applied issue and UP-413 terminology proposal updated Consent category-code definitions, confirming Advance Directive category examples are now terminology-maintained rather than Consent.scope text.
Open 2025+ question about treatment directives and Advance Directives across Consent, ServiceRequest, PACIO, and IPS; not a final source-change decision for this reconciliation.
